title: Nonmembership after one additional step
statement: Let $K,L,v$ be natural numbers, let $R$ be a binary relation on the natural numbers, and let $I$ be a predicate on the natural numbers, and suppose $v<K$. The vertex $v$ is not reachable in at most $L+1$ steps from any $I$-vertex below $K$ if and only if every vertex $u$ reachable in at most $L$ steps from such a starting vertex is distinct from $v$ and does not satisfy $R(u,v)$.
hypotheses_covered: $R$ is a binary relation on the natural numbers
$I$ is a predicate on the natural numbers
